validated_results.title: Alcohol intake, drinking patterns, and prostate cancer risk and mortality: a 30-year prospective cohort study of Finnish twins.
validated_results.reason: Prospective 30-year cohort of Finnish twins reporting incident prostate cancer risk in relation to midlife alcohol intake and drinking patterns, providing a population-wide exposure estimate.

extraction.comparison_type: Heavy drinkers (>14 drinks/week) vs light drinkers (≤3 drinks/week; non-abstainers)
extraction.population: Population-based cohort of Finnish male twins followed from 1981 to 2012

sample_size.excerpt: Data were drawn from the Older Finnish Twin Cohort and included 11,372 twins followed from 1981 to 2012.

cases.excerpt: Over the study period, 601 incident cases of prostate cancer and 110 deaths from prostate cancer occurred.

effect_size.excerpt: Compared to light drinkers (≤3 drinks/week; non-abstainers), heavy drinkers (>14 drinks/week) were at a 1.46-fold higher risk (HR 1.46; 95 % CI 1.12, 1.91) of prostate cancer, adjusting for important confounders.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared to light drinkers (≤3 drinks/week; non-abstainers), heavy drinkers (>14 drinks/week) were at a 1.46-fold higher risk (HR 1.46; 95 % CI 1.12, 1.91) of prostate cancer, adjusting for important confounders.

comparison.excerpt: Compared to light drinkers (≤3 drinks/week; non-abstainers), heavy drinkers (>14 drinks/week)

design.excerpt: a 30-year prospective cohort study of Finnish twins

timing.excerpt: We aimed to prospectively investigate the association between midlife alcohol intake

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Alcohol consumption was assessed by questionnaires administered at two time points over follow-up.
